quests.instruction: The letters s and h team up to make one sound: /sh/. Which word begins with /sh/?
quests.hint: Hush! Put a finger to your lips and make that quiet sound. Which word starts with it?
quests.explanation: “Ship” starts with /sh/. “Sip” starts with /s/ and “chip” starts with /ch/.
quests.funFact: The word “shh” is just the /sh/ sound by itself.

quests.instruction: “Fish” has four letters. How many separate sounds do you tap out?
quests.hint: Tap one finger for each sound. Remember that sh makes only one sound.
quests.explanation: “Fish” has 3 sounds: /f/ /i/ /sh/. It has 4 letters, but s and h work together as one digraph.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with /sh/?
quests.hint: Listen to how each word ends. Which one finishes with a hush?
quests.explanation: “Dish” ends with /sh/. “Dig” ends with /g/ and “did” ends with /d/.

quests.instruction: Which two letters team up to make the first sound of “chin”?
quests.hint: Chug like a train: ch-ch-ch. Which two letters write that sound?
quests.explanation: The letters c and h make one sound, /ch/, at the start of “chin”.
quests.funFact: A group of two letters that makes one sound is called a digraph.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with /ch/?
quests.hint: Listen to the last sound of each word. Only one finishes with a chug.
quests.explanation: “Much” ends with /ch/. “Mush” ends with /sh/ and “must” ends with /t/.
quests.funFact: Chug, chip, chair and cheese all start with the /ch/ digraph.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? Mom will __op the onions.
quests.hint: Say each choice and test it in the sentence.
quests.explanation: “Chop” fits the sentence. “Shop” is a real word too, but it does not make sense here.

quests.instruction: “Thumb” starts with a sound made with your tongue between your teeth. Which two letters write it?
quests.hint: Poke your tongue between your teeth and blow softly.
quests.explanation: “Thumb” starts with /th/, written with the digraph th.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with /th/?
quests.hint: Listen to the last sound. Does your tongue peek out at the end?
quests.explanation: “Bath” ends with /th/. “Bat” ends with /t/ and “back” ends with /k/.

quests.instruction: Which word starts with /th/, where your tongue peeks out?
quests.hint: Say each word and watch your tongue in a mirror.
quests.explanation: “Thin” starts with /th/. “Tin” starts with /t/ and “fin” starts with /f/.
quests.funFact: Thin and tin only differ in their first sound, and so do thin and fin.

quests.instruction: The th in “this” buzzes, but the th in “thin” is quiet. Which word has the buzzing th?
quests.hint: Put a finger on your throat. Which word makes it buzz at the start?
quests.explanation: “That” has the voiced th, /th/ with a buzz. “Thick” and “thumb” have the quiet th.

quests.instruction: Which word starts with the same th sound as “then”?
quests.hint: Start with “then” and feel your throat. Does it buzz? Match that.
quests.explanation: “Then” and “them” both have the buzzing th. “Thin” and “think” have the quiet th.

quests.instruction: Which word has the quiet /th/ at the start?
quests.hint: Say each word with a hand on your throat. The quiet one gives no buzz.
quests.explanation: “Three” has the quiet th. “This” and “they” both buzz.
quests.funFact: Small words like the, this, that, then and they all have the buzzing th.

quests.instruction: Which letter pair starts “whale”?
quests.hint: Round your lips like you are blowing a candle out.
quests.explanation: “Whale” starts with the digraph wh, which sounds like /w/ for most speakers.
quests.funFact: Wh words like whale, wheel and when start with /w/ for most speakers, though some people say /hw/.

quests.instruction: The letters ph can make the /f/ sound. Which word begins with /f/ spelled ph?
quests.hint: Look for the word that begins with ph, not just any word that begins with /f/.
quests.explanation: “Phone” starts with /f/ spelled ph. “Fun” also starts with /f/, but spells it with f.
quests.funFact: Phone, photo and elephant all use ph for /f/. Many of these words come from Greek.

quests.instruction: Which word spells its ending /f/ sound with ph?
quests.hint: All three words end with /f/. Look at the letters at the end.
quests.explanation: “Graph” ends with ph. “Staff” and “stuff” spell /f/ with ff.

quests.instruction: Which letters make the ending sound in “ring”?
quests.hint: Say ring and hold the last sound. It rings through your nose.
quests.explanation: The letters n and g make one sound, /ng/, at the end of “ring”.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with /ng/?
quests.hint: Listen to the last sound of each word. Which one hums at the back of your throat?
quests.explanation: “Song” ends with /ng/. “Sock” ends with /k/ and “sun” ends with /n/.

quests.instruction: How many letters and how many sounds are in “wing”?
quests.hint: Count the letters first. Then tap out the sounds: /w/, /i/, and the ng sound.
quests.explanation: “Wing” has 4 letters but only 3 sounds: /w/ /i/ /ng/. The n and g make one sound together.
quests.funFact: In /ng/, you do not hear a separate /g/ at the end of sing, ring or wing.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with the /k/ sound spelled ck?
quests.hint: Listen for a click at the end. Then check the letters.
quests.explanation: “Duck” ends with /k/ spelled ck. “Dug” ends with /g/ and “dust” ends with /t/.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? so__ (you wear it on your foot)
quests.hint: Think of the word. Which two letters write the ending sound?
quests.explanation: “Sock” ends with ck, which makes one /k/ sound after a short vowel.
quests.funFact: The ck spelling usually comes right after a short vowel, like in back, neck and kick.

quests.instruction: Which word spells its final /k/ sound with ck?
quests.hint: Check how each word ends. Two end with a single k.
quests.explanation: “Kick” ends with ck. “Milk” and “book” end with a single k.

quests.instruction: Which word starts with a different sound from the others?
quests.hint: Compare the first sounds. Two of these begin with a hush.
quests.explanation: “Shop” and “ship” start with /sh/. “Chop” starts with /ch/.
quests.funFact: The digraph ch usually says /ch/, but in a few words, like chef, it says /sh/.

quests.instruction: Where do you hear /ch/ in “bench”?
quests.hint: Say the word slowly and listen to the very last sound.
quests.explanation: “Bench” ends with /ch/. The sounds are /b/ /e/ /n/ /ch/.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with the same sound as “bath”?
quests.hint: Listen for your tongue peeking out at the end.
quests.explanation: “Bath” and “moth” both end with /th/. “Mop” ends with /p/ and “mom” ends with /m/.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? __ell — you can find one on the beach.
quests.hint: Say each choice and see which makes a real word.
quests.explanation: “Shell” starts with /sh/. “Chell” and “thell” are not real words.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? ba__ — you take one in the tub.
quests.hint: Think of the word for washing in the tub, then pick the ending.
quests.explanation: “Bath” ends with th. “Bash” and “back” are real words, but they do not fit the clue.
quests.funFact: In “bath”, th is quiet, but in “bathe” it is voiced, so it buzzes.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? __ale — a huge animal that lives in the sea.
quests.hint: Remember that this digraph sounds like /w/.
quests.explanation: “Whale” starts with wh. “Chale” and “thale” are not words.

quests.instruction: Which word has exactly 3 sounds?
quests.hint: Count the sounds, not the letters. A digraph counts as one sound.
quests.explanation: “Chip” has 3 sounds: /ch/ /i/ /p/. “Chimp” has 4 sounds and “chips” has 4 sounds.

quests.instruction: Which sound do the letters ph make in “dolphin”?
quests.hint: Say dolphin out loud and listen to the middle of the word.
quests.explanation: In “dolphin”, the ph makes /f/. The word has the sounds /d/ /o/ /l/ /f/ /i/ /n/.

quests.instruction: Which word does NOT contain a digraph?
quests.hint: Look for letter pairs that make one sound.
quests.explanation: “Dish” has sh and “duck” has ck. “Dig” has three letters that make three sounds.
quests.funFact: Not every pair of consonants is a digraph. In a digraph, two letters make only one sound.
